---
title: "PCA from First Principles"
---

This project develops an understanding of principal component analysis
through mathematical explanations, worked examples, and reproducible
Python code.

## Approach

Each lecture will connect a concrete question to the mathematical
objects, operations, and assumptions needed to answer it. Accompanying
Python examples will make the reasoning executable and inspectable.

## Lectures

1. [What Does It Mean to Represent Something Mathematically?](lectures/01-mathematical-representation/index.qmd) — Objects, measurements, labels, and the meaning of numerical relationships.

2. [From a Scalar to a List of Measurements](lectures/02-scalars-and-measurements/index.qmd) — Scalar values, ordered observations, mixed units, and semantic Python types.

3. [How Measurements Become a Space](lectures/03-measurements-become-space/index.qmd) — Dimensions, points, coordinates, reference frames, and displacement.

4. [What Exactly Is a Vector?](lectures/04-vectors-components-scaling/index.qmd) — Points, displacements, vector operations, and coordinate representations.

5. [Direction and Its Standard Vector Representative](lectures/05-direction-and-standard-representatives/index.qmd) — Magnitude, orientation, shared directions, and why a standard representative is useful.

6. [Normalization and the Reasoning Behind Algebraic Steps](lectures/06-normalization-and-algebraic-reasoning/index.qmd) — Reciprocal scaling, factor isolation, direction preservation, and reconstruction.

7. [Coordinates and Reference Systems](lectures/07-coordinates-and-reference-systems/index.qmd) - Origins, basis vectors, signed decomposition coefficients, and representing one fixed vector in two bases. 

8. [Lecture 8 — From Basis Decomposition to Matrix Multiplication](lectures/08-basis-decomposition-and-matrices/index.qmd)

9. [Observations as Data Vectors](lectures/09-observations-as-data-vectors/index.qmd) — Stage 3 begins with measurement schemas, observation vectors, feature differences, and dataset rows and columns.

10. [Dataset vs Feature Space](lectures/10-dataset-and-feature-space/index.qmd) — Observation count, feature dimension, aggregation axes, and dataset-wide structure.

11. [Why Do We Need a New Reference Point?](lectures/11-mean-as-reference/index.qmd) — The mean as a collective reference, signed deviations, and reconstruction.

12. [What Centering Changes and What It Preserves](lectures/12-centering-reference-change/index.qmd) — Reference changes, preserved displacements, broadcasting, and the limits of signed averages.

## Project status

The first 12 conceptual lectures include executable Python companions. Automated checks validate Python formatting, semantic types, package imports, feature-space and spatial-vector relationships, and website rendering. PCA algorithms and their tests will follow as the lectures develop.

## Source code

The source files and development history are available in the
